scenario: CloudKeep, a processor for retailer Bryce Co., signed a data-processing agreement and began using a new sub-processor, ByteHaul, for backups. CloudKeep emailed Bryce Co. about adding ByteHaul 14 days before the change, and Bryce Co. never raised an objection.
policy: A data processor may engage a sub-processor only if it has the controller's prior written authorization. A general written authorization permitting sub-processors satisfies this requirement provided the controller is informed of any intended changes and does not object.
question: Was CloudKeep's engagement of ByteHaul authorized under the policy?
